title: Why Is This English Wall So Wiggly?
description:
Why are some old English garden walls wiggly? These crinkle-crankle walls are only one brick thick, yet they stand on their own. A straight wall that thin would blow over: it would need to be two bricks thick, plus pillars. In a wavy wall every curve braces the next one, like a folded sheet of paper standing on its edge, so the wall stands without pillars and can use fewer bricks overall. The curves also catch the sun, making warm, sheltered pockets for fruit trees.

Wiggly or straight: which wall would you build?
